text:
kim: quick heads-up — I ran a batch of perf tests on Mixtral (head_dim=150) and hit a nasty divergence when FlashAttention is selected. long seqs (2048) produce NaNs during decode.
jason: can you paste the profiler output / a minimal repro? which kernel path was picked?
kim: profiler shows kernel_selector chose flash (because favor_flash=true). reproducer: single-stream decode on 2048 tokens with kv cache warm. numbers below.
kim: profiling snippets:\n```
model: mixtral-7b
head_dim: 150
seq_len: 2048
batch: 1
profiles:
  sdpa: 5.1 ms/token
  flash (force pad->160): 3.2 ms/token
  flash (no pad): crash (NaN) at step ~512
```
anita: ugh. head_dim not multiple of 8/16 is tricky for flash kernels — we normally either pad at load time or route to sdpa/triton. did the crash include a mask-related stack trace?
kim: yes. stack points at flashattention mask gather step. mask values get shifted and we end up applying invalid attention weights. logs show invalid memory read in kernel.
sandeep: lighting up memory: one suspect is KV cache layout/stride assumptions between kernels. when we fallback mid-session (e.g., flash->sdpa) we might not normalize the KV layout/padding, causing mis-indexing.
kim: I saw exactly that: we did an autoscale-based fallback when latency spiked, and subsequent requests that reused a session saw misaligned KV reads.
tina: two separate issues then — 1) flash kernel mask implementation for non-padded heads, 2) inconsistent KV cache format between kernels. both can create NaNs.
jason: proposals:
  - detect head_dim % 8 != 0 early and choose safe kernel (sdpa/triton) by default unless we explicitly pad.
  - implement an in-memory padding shim for KV cache (zero-pad head axis to next multiple) so flash can be used without model-level recompile.
  - add a kernel compatibility handshake: runtime advertises cache_layout and kernels must accept/convert or runtime converts.
anita: prefer the shim + handshake. padding at runtime keeps throughput benefits and lets us drop into flash for most workloads. downside: extra memory and one-time copy on session init.
sandeep: note: copying the KV pad after every step is expensive. do it once on session start and track a cache_format flag on Session: {layout: "packed_headpad_160", padded_heads: 10}.
kim: sketch of a minimal check in kernel selection code:\n```
if (head_dim % 8 != 0) {
  if (config.runtime_headpad) {
    pad_kv_cache_to(next_multiple(head_dim,8));
    select_kernel("flash");
  } else {
    select_kernel("sdpa");
  }
}
```
jason: also add an invariant check before every decode chunk: verify KV offsets and shape. fail early and convert rather than letting the kernel corrupt state.
tina: another tangent: RoPE scaling on Mixtral we saw earlier bumps fp16 mantissa issues in flash kernels for very long sequences. we should clamp rotary scales and maybe compute some ops in fp32 inside the flash kernel when scale>1.
anita: agree. add a quick guard: if (roper_scale > 1.5f) use fp32 path or route to sdpa. silently downgrading precision caused subtle quality regressions.
kim: test plan I ran:
  - unit: head_dim 1..256 stepping, kernel_selector toggles, 500 random prompts
  - integration: canary on dedicated pool with padded shim enabled
results: padded-flash gives best perf but +8% VRAM cost. sdpa stable but 40% slower on token throughput.
ci-bot: CI: added tests for head_padding and cache_format conversion. link: https://ci.internal/redwood/build/7892 (tests pass)
deploy-bot: canary deploying runtime v0.72.3 to eng-runtime-canary with runtime_headpad=true
sandeep: action items:
  - kim: implement session cache_format flag + conversion (PR)
  - anita: add unit tests for kernel mask correctness across head dims
  - tina: add RoPE scale guards and a small fp32 fallback in flash kernel
  - jason: add invariant checks and a runtime metric for 'kernel_cache_format_mismatch'
  target: EOD + 3 business days for full regression run.
kim: I'll open a draft PR tonight and include perf traces and mem delta.
jason: once PRs land, let's canary for 24h and check token error rates + latency p50/p95.
anita: also add a fallback route policy: if flash returns NaN or kernel error, do not reuse session state — force new session creation to avoid persistent corrupted cache.
kim: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
